{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-me-c","lineage":{"candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-me-class-c:lineage:39","input_manifest_sha256":"e58e81684e1620cd41b012f43e58952755f7a64a88f1c52f2f1ca04bfe0c1e07","source_registry_sha256":"c2e42c38f9f4644827a2fdadadd6340aab123a85c208ecc4839848339c6c9a98","source_liveness_sha256":"e742bf2373c9a6bebd7774b2b45ae2a58ba395947586ea942f331e99a0744f40"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Avoiding Crashes","heading":"C — Avoiding Crashes","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Avoiding Crashes

FACT_ID: sec09-F01 | anchor: A94
Braking, steering and acceleration are the manual’s three possible ways to avoid a collision or lessen its impact. [A94]
Source: [A94 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec09-F02 | anchor: A94
Antilock brakes help maintain steering control during a stop. [A94]
Source: [A94 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec09-F03 | anchor: A94
Read the vehicle owner’s manual for instructions on using its antilock braking system. [A94]
Source: [A94 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec09-F04 | anchor: A94
An ABS pedal can vibrate and the system can make a clicking sound during operation. [A94]
Source: [A94 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec09-F05 | anchor: A94
For a vehicle without ABS, consult its owner’s manual for the appropriate braking method. [A94]
Source: [A94 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec09-F06 | anchor: A94
If a collision cannot be avoided by stopping in time, steering around the hazard may provide an escape. [A94]
Source: [A94 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec09-F07 | anchor: A94
When steering around a hazard, avoid braking during the turn if possible, particularly when entering a soft shoulder. [A94]
Source: [A94 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec09-F08 | anchor: A95
For a quick steering response, hold opposite sides of the wheel at 9 and 3 or 8 and 4. [A95]
Source: [A95 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec09-F09 | anchor: A95
After steering clear of an obstacle, countersteer toward the original lane and remain ready for another correction. [A95]
Source: [A95 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec09-F10 | anchor: A95
Grip the wheel with both hands when making an emergency steering maneuver. [A95]
Source: [A95 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec09-F11 | anchor: A95
Choose an escape direction that avoids other traffic, then straighten and reduce speed after clearing the hazard. [A95]
Source: [A95 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec09-F12 | anchor: A95
A swerve can lead to a second collision, so watch the escape path as well as the initial obstacle. [A95]
Source: [A95 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec09-F13 | anchor: A95
Acceleration may sometimes avoid a vehicle about to strike from the side or rear. [A95]
Source: [A95 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec09-F14 | anchor: A95
For that acceleration escape, a manual-transmission vehicle may need a downshift; the automatic-transmission example uses the accelerator. [A95]
Source: [A95 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec09-F15 | anchor: A95
Reading printed material while driving is prohibited, with a map and written directions to a particular destination excluded from that definition. [A95]
Source: [A95 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec09-F16 | anchor: A95
If a rear impact is imminent, be prepared to brake so the vehicle is not pushed into one ahead. [A95]
Source: [A95 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec09-F17 | anchor: A95
If a side impact spins the vehicle, be ready to steer to try to regain control. [A95]
Source: [A95 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec09-F18 | anchor: A96
After a crash, stop immediately, assist injured people as possible and arrange an ambulance when needed. [A96]
Source: [A96 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec09-F19 | anchor: A96
Do not move an injured person unless another danger requires moving them to safety. [A96]
Source: [A96 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec09-F20 | anchor: A96
The manual directs involved drivers to remain at the crash scene until police arrive and question those involved. [A96]
Source: [A96 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec09-F21 | anchor: A96
Move the crashed vehicle out of the traffic path if you can do so. [A96]
Source: [A96 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec09-F22 | anchor: A96
Collect names and addresses for everyone involved, injured people and witnesses. [A96]
Source: [A96 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec09-F23 | anchor: A96
Record the other driver’s name, address and license number, checking that the name matches the license. [A96]
Source: [A96 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec09-F24 | anchor: A96
Record the other vehicle’s make, model, year and plate number, its damage and the insurance company’s name. [A96]
Source: [A96 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec09-F25 | anchor: A96
Document when and where the crash occurred and the vehicles’ and pedestrians’ positions and travel directions before and after it. [A96]
Source: [A96 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec09-F26 | anchor: A96
Record poor weather or road conditions relevant to the crash. [A96]
Source: [A96 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec09-F27 | anchor: A96
Contact police for a crash involving injury and give factual information about the event. [A96]
Source: [A96 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec09-F28 | anchor: A96
If you damage a parked vehicle, try to locate its owner; if unsuccessful, leave a note where the owner can find it. [A96]
Source: [A96 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec09-F29 | anchor: A96
The parked-vehicle note should identify you by name, address, driver-license number and plate, and give the crash date, time and damage description. [A96]
Source: [A96 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec09-F30 | anchor: A96
The pinned manual requires a report to police or the local sheriff for any crash injury or property damage of at least $2,000. [A96]
Source: [A96 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec09-F31 | anchor: A96
Failing to report a reportable crash can lead to criminal charges and suspension of the driver’s license. [A96]
Source: [A96 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec09-F32 | anchor: A96
For an otherwise nonreportable crash injuring or killing a dog, cat or livestock, take reasonable steps to notify the owner or, if unavailable, law enforcement or animal control. [A96]
Source: [A96 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec09-F33 | anchor: A97
When emergency medical responders are already at a crash, follow their instructions and keep attention on the road and traffic officers. [A97]
Source: [A97 -> pdf-0097]

Misconceptions: emergency avoidance can involve steering or acceleration as well as braking. [A94]
Mnemonic: observe, choose an escape, maintain control, seek help.
Glossary: ABS means antilock braking system. [A94]
Dynamic facts: contradictory braking instructions, medical techniques and equipment procedures require verification.
